name: Interactive rebase
about: Reorder, squash and drop commits from a panel, without the todo file
_about: git rebase -i works by writing a todo list and opening your editor on
it. This keeps that arrangement and replaces the part where you edit a
file about your commits with a panel of your commits.
Then `rebase` in the palette, or Alt-2. p r e s f d set what happens to
the commit you are on, [ and ] move it, x runs it.
The trick is GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR. git asks for the todo file to be
edited; the editor it is given is `cp our-plan`, which replaces it with
the one this plugin wrote. Nothing here re-implements any part of what
Where it stops: a rebase that hits a conflict wants files resolved and
`git rebase --continue`. This opens the files git named and gives you c
and a for continue and abort, but resolving the conflict is you and the
editor. Conflict resolution is its own project and pretending otherwise
here would be worse than saying so.
